target.statement: ZEN mean AUROC (×100) over the 47 ADBench datasets in the contaminated regime = 79.7

compute.basis: ZEN requires ~3,750 s of A100 time per seed for 47 datasets (Table 17: 850 s + 2,904 s), i.e. ~5 GPU-hours per seed and ~25 GPU-hours for 5 seeds; on a CPU-only laptop TabPFN forward passes are ~10-20x slower, pushing the full protocol to many hours to days, and the paper itself states both ZEN and FOCUS 'need a GPU'.

blockers: Paper explicitly states ZEN/FOCUS need a GPU; TabPFN-3 forward passes over 10-fold leave-one-out x 6 feature subsets x 47 datasets x 5 seeds are far too slow on 8 CPU cores
Full headline number averages over 47 datasets and 5 seeds, not a single small run
TabPFN-3 checkpoint (tabpfn 8.1.0) is large and must be downloaded; CPU inference is the bottleneck
Reproducing the exact 79.7 requires the full ADBench pipeline with the authors' leak fix and per-dataset configs
title: Adapting prior-data fitted networks for tabular anomaly detection
